newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Inter-Korean Red Cross talks proposal stalled.
newsitem.headline: Inter-Korean Red Cross talks proposal stalled.

text.p: North Korea's Red Cross on Monday again rejected a proposal by its Southern counterpart that talks on speeding up food aid be held in the border village of Panmunjom.
The proposal for talks was first made by the head of the South Korean Red Cross, Kang Young-hoon, on April 18.
The Northern side said it would welcome talks and proposed May 3. But it insisted discussions be held in Beijing.
In a reply last Thursday, Kang said there was no need for Koreans to meet in a third country and proposed a working-level session in Panmunjom on Tuesday.
On Monday, the North Korean Red Cross reiterated its earlier position in a message relayed via a telephone "hot line" at Panmunjom, the South Korea Red Cross said in a statement.
South and North Korea remain technically at war after their 1950-53 conflict ended in a truce.
North Korea is on the edge of famine after two consecutive years of devastating floods.
